title: House-Hunting Photographer Spots Hidden Key, Steals Rs 55-Lakh Gold From Bengaluru Techie's Flat | Bengaluru-news News - News18
text: Are you in the habit of hiding your house keys in shoe racks or flower pots outside the entrance? If so, you may want to ditch the practice and instead make enough copies of the keys for all house mates. A software engineer’s family in Bengaluru’s Whitefield found this out the hard way after a freelance photographer spotted their key hiding place during a house hunting visit and later used it to steal 348 grams of gold from the flat. According to local reports, the accused, 42-year-old Kiran, is a resident of Varthur Kodi and used to run a photo studio, which later shut down, forcing him to take up odd assignments as a wedding photographer. During a visit to the residential society in Nagondanahalli to look for a flat, he reportedly spotted the software engineer tucking in the house keys in the shoe rack outside the entrance for his children to use later after school. According to police, on February 11, the software engineer locked the door and left the keys in the shoe rack. Later in the evening, he found the door of the flat open and 348 grams of gold jewellery, worth Rs 55 lakh, missing from a cupboard. He approached the police who immediately went through the CCTV footage and traced Kiran near Varthur Kodi. The accused was arrested on February 13 and allegedly confessed to the crime. A report in the Times of India quoted police commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh as saying that residents should not leave their keys in places easily accessible to strangers.
